title: Tapping Neighbourhood Shops and Minimarts as Social Enterprises
what_it_is: Tapping Neighbourhood Shops and Minimarts as Social Enterprises

sections.label: Community food support partnerships
sections.summary: Community partners provide meals, rations and perishables, complementing Government services like Meals-on-Wheels and appointed vendors for Long-Term Assistance clients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: For example, community partners are involved in providing cooked meals, dry rations and perishables to eligible clients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Some are run in partnership with hawker stall owners and local merchants, and offer lower prices due to support from donors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: These efforts complement Government efforts such as the Ministry of Health's Meals-on-Wheels service which provides subsidised meal deliveries to eligible homebound clients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Social and Family Development has also appointed vendors to ensure that our clients on Long-Term Assistance receive the supplies they need to meet their specific needs.
